content:
**Fixed lane collector over-reporting collected count on re-run (#887 C1)**

**What**: `collectLane()` in `brain/scripts/memory/lane/collect.mjs` returned `plan.files.length` as `collected`, and used the same count in the commit subject's `(N records)`. Fixed to derive both from `git diff-tree -r --name-only --no-commit-id <parentTree> <newTree>` — the set of paths that actually changed between the commit this run builds on and the tree it just wrote.

**Why (root cause)**: `plan.files` is `lane/plan.mjs`'s per-run group-WINNER list, recomputed fresh from every candidate still sitting untracked on disk in each worktree — it says nothing about whether that winner is already committed to the lane ref's current tip. The planner's only "is this already known" filter is `mainPaths` (`git ls-tree origin/main`), never the lane ref itself (by design — the planner is pure and never reads the ref). So on a same-day re-run, a file collected in an earlier run of the same day re-enters `plan.files` unchanged (still untracked on disk, still absent from origin/main), and the old code counted it again. Measured directly with a fixture: one genuinely new file on a re-run reported `collected: 3` instead of `1` (2 stale group-winners + 1 new).

**Where**: `brain/scripts/memory/lane/collect.mjs` (the fix, between `write-tree` and `commit-tree`), `brain/scripts/memory/lane/collect.integration.test.mjs` (B1.4 extended with `second.collected === 1` and a commit-subject match, RED-confirmed against the old code before the fix, 3 !== 1).

**Learned**: The planner (`plan.mjs`) stays pure and untouched — the fix lives entirely in the IO shell as a tree-diff read, which was the smaller of two options a cold review offered (the other being to teach the planner about the ref's tip via an extra "already-in-lane" path set). A tree-diff between parent and new tree is the only reliable source of "what changed" once a pure per-run planner is deliberately kept ignorant of the ref's own history.
